Jio Platforms Sets Stage for October 28 Listing Following ₹10.3 Lakh Crore IPO Valuation

29 Oct 2026, 10:30 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Business Desk · Source: news.abplive.com

Market Debut and Valuation Milestones

Jio Platforms is scheduled to list on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. The digital services and telecom company enters the public markets following an initial public offering (IPO) that established a valuation of ₹10.3 lakh crore. According to pre-listing highlights, the offering marks the first instance of an Indian company launching a public debut at a valuation exceeding ₹10 lakh crore.

For the IPO, the company issued 27 crore new shares priced at ₹1,119 per share. This initial valuation places Jio Platforms as India's fourth-largest company by market capitalisation. It trails Reliance Industries, which is valued at ₹16.2 lakh crore, Bharti Airtel at ₹12.2 lakh crore, and HDFC Bank at ₹10.6 lakh crore.

Potential Market Shifts and Conglomerate Rankings

Market participants and grey market indicators have pointed toward the possibility of strong demand and a listing premium. Observers note that if shares debut at a 20% premium over the allotment price of ₹1,119, they would trade near ₹1,340 per share. Such a premium could elevate Jio Platforms' market capitalisation beyond ₹12.3 lakh crore, positioning it as India's second-most valuable listed corporation behind Reliance Industries.

The combined valuation of Reliance Industries and Jio Platforms at the IPO price exceeds ₹27 lakh crore. This combined figure places the Reliance Group, led by Mukesh Ambani, ahead of other major domestic business houses. For comparison, the 32 publicly listed companies under the Tata Group held a combined market capitalisation of approximately ₹25.7 lakh crore as of October 27, 2026, while the 11 listed Adani Group companies were valued at around ₹16.6 lakh crore. A potential listing price of ₹1,340 per share could push the combined Reliance footprint closer to ₹30 lakh crore, though final standings will depend entirely on actual exchange trading.

Practical Implications and Verification

For investors and market analysts, the primary focus shifts to how the stock performs during its opening trading sessions on October 28. While grey market trends suggest a potential premium, actual trading prices on the NSE and BSE will dictate the definitive market capitalization and corporate rankings.

Readers seeking to verify details of the listing, official exchange filings, and final market performance can review the original report published by ABP Live at https://news.abplive.com/business/jio-platforms-ipo-10-3-lakh-crore-valuation-sets-stage-for-october-28-listing-1873415. Official stock exchange websites (NSE and BSE) provide real-time updates on share prices, trading volumes, and official market capitalisation figures following the opening bell.
